about: Evaluation questions. Expected facts were located with scripts/find_in_papers.py by the assistant on 2026-11-11 and must be checked by the user before grading (user_verified).

grading_rubric.correct: Answerable question; answer states every key fact (or a faithful paraphrase), adds no claim contradicted by or absent from the papers, and at least one citation points to a listed expected location (paper + section, or paper + page).
grading_rubric.wrong: Answerable question; a key fact is missing or wrong, OR an unsupported claim is added, OR no citation points to an expected location. Also: an unanswerable question that the system answered instead of refusing.
grading_rubric.refused_correctly: Unanswerable question; the system says the papers do not contain the answer and makes no factual claim about it.
grading_rubric.refused_wrongly: Answerable question; the system refused or said the papers do not say.

questions.question: In the Transformer's multi-head attention, how many heads are used and what are the per-head key and value dimensions?
key_facts: h = 8 heads
d_k = d_v = d_model/h = 64

questions.question: Why does the Transformer scale the dot products by 1/sqrt(d_k)?
key_facts: for large d_k the dot products grow large in magnitude
this pushes the softmax into regions with extremely small gradients

questions.question: What hardware was the Transformer trained on, and how long did one training step take for the base model?
key_facts: one machine with 8 NVIDIA P100 GPUs
about 0.4 seconds per step for the base models

questions.question: What label smoothing value did the Transformer use, and what effect did it have?
key_facts: epsilon_ls = 0.1
hurts perplexity (model learns to be more unsure)
improves accuracy and BLEU

questions.trap: paraphrase: the question never says 'positional encoding'
questions.question: How does the Transformer know the order of the words in a sentence, and did a learned alternative work better?
key_facts: sinusoidal positional encodings added to the input embeddings
learned positional embeddings gave nearly identical results (Table 3 row E)

questions.trap: table: the results table row is filed under §5.4 by the parser and loses its column labels
questions.question: What BLEU score does the Transformer achieve on WMT 2014 English-to-French?
key_facts: 41.8 BLEU (single model, big Transformer)

questions.question: What is the frame rate of the Mimi codec, and how many quantizers does it use?
key_facts: Q = 8 quantizers
codebook size 2048 (1.1 kbps)

questions.question: What latency does Moshi achieve?
key_facts: theoretical latency 160 ms
200 ms in practice

questions.question: What is Helium and how much data was it pretrained on?
key_facts: 7B-parameter text LLM
pretrained on 2.1T tokens of public English data

questions.question: What is Inner Monologue in Moshi and why is it used?
key_facts: predicts time-aligned text tokens before (as a prefix to) audio tokens
improves factuality and linguistic quality of generated speech

questions.trap: multi-paper: needs one passage from each paper
questions.question: Which positional encoding does Moshi's Helium model use, and how does that differ from the original Transformer?
key_facts: Helium uses rotary positional embeddings (RoPE)
the original Transformer uses sinusoidal positional encodings

questions.question: How does H-Net's routing module decide where chunk boundaries are?
key_facts: cosine similarity between adjacent encoder outputs
converted into boundary probabilities p_t (low similarity -> boundary)
p_1 = 1 so the sequence starts with a boundary

questions.question: What is the purpose of the ratio loss in H-Net?
key_facts: guides compression toward a target compression ratio N
uses F (fraction of vectors selected) and G (average boundary probability)
inspired by load balancing in Mixture-of-Experts

questions.question: What kind of layers does H-Net use for its encoder and decoder networks, and why?
key_facts: Mamba-2 layers
state space models excel at fine-grained data (audio, DNA, robotic control)

questions.trap: the abstract says 'nearly 4x' while the introduction says 3.6x for DNA
questions.question: Where is H-Net's advantage over tokenized models largest, and by how much?
key_facts: languages/modalities without obvious segmentation cues: Chinese, code, DNA
XWinograd-zh 59.9 -> 66.3
DNA: 3.6x data efficiency vs isotropic models (abstract: nearly 4x)

questions.question: What does the smoothing module in H-Net's dynamic chunking do?
key_facts: interpolates representations using the router's outputs
attenuates the effect of uncertain boundaries, improving learnability
